rail_guard.text: Aberystwyth, end of the line for the Cambrian, start of the line for everything else.
Tickets? Hop on. The Wildlore rail runs to any town you have visited. Where to?

cliff_op.text: Aberystwyth Cliff Railway, 1896. Longest electric cliff railway in Britain.
Two cars, one cable, balanced like a see-saw. The car going up pulls the car coming down. Physics!

then.text: Raining? Ice cream still tastes the same, cariad. Wetter, but the same.
Gale's up! Hold that cone with both hands. The seagulls are using the wind for extra speed.
Sunshine on the prom! Queue starts here. The seagulls are already at the front.

ice_cream.text: {greeting} Mint choc chip, Welsh honey or 99 with a flake. Pick quickly, a seagull is already looking.
Last Tuesday one took a whole cone out of a toddler's hand. Now it has a regular spot. Business model.

then.text: Dusk! This is it. Watch the pier. Any minute the sky will fill with starlings. Well, now in a minute.
Fog over the bay. The starlings will still find the pier. They're cleverer than my satnav.

starling_man.text: Come back in winter at dusk. Thousands of starlings roost under the Royal Pier.
They swirl like smoke and then, whoosh, they all vanish under the boards. Best free show in Wales.

then.text: Drizzle again. I'll go to my lecture in a minute. After a cup of tea. And maybe a scone.
Dawn over Cardigan Bay. I'm only up because I haven't been to bed. Essay deadline.

student_aber.text: It's the Old College, the first building of the university. Gothic revival, with a courtyard and echoes.
I came for the degree. I stayed for the cliff railway. Don't tell my tutor.

librarian.text: The National Library of Wales gets a free copy of every book published in the UK. It's called legal deposit.
It's lovely. It's also heavy. The staff have excellent arms.

fisher_aber.text: Aber means 'mouth of the river'. Ystwyth plus aber. Aberystwyth. See?
Rivers meet the sea here. I meet the fish less often.

then.text: Gale on the prom! Waves over the railings. Kick the bar quick and run, that's my advice.
Lovely day for walking the whole prom. Don't forget to kick the bar at the end.

prom_walker.text: {greeting} Kicking the Bar is a tradition. You walk the whole prom and kick the railing at the far end.
Students do it in Freshers' week. Beginners kick it in the wrong direction, usually.

aberystwyth_crab_warden.text: Crabbing's a tradition on this wall: a line, a bucket, a bit of bacon and a great deal of patience. The rule never changes. Every crab goes back.
